section_summary: This section records Japanese fishing and research vessels operating near Alaska in 1936, including crab canneries and the training ship Hakuyo Maru. It documents arrangements for visits to Aleutian ports, the cancellation of the Hakuho Maru’s visit, and Coast Guard observations. A Bureau of Fisheries report and an attached trade journal article express concern that Japanese vessels might begin catching Bristol Bay salmon beyond U.S. territorial waters.

subfiles.title: Despatch concerning Japanese crab-fishing vessels
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports assurances that Japanese vessels bound for the Bering Sea will conduct familiar operations and will not fish for salmon.
subfiles.summary: Closing page of Grew’s despatch, introducing an enclosed Foreign Office letter.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office letter listing crab-fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Lists the Toten Maru, Taihoku Maru, and accessory boats departing Hakodate for Bering Sea crab fishing and allied operations.
subfiles.summary: Togo says the vessels will operate on the high seas and avoid American waters; fish meal will be the Taihoku Maru’s principal product.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Tokyo despatch to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew’s despatch and Togo’s letter on two Japanese crab-fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of the Tokyo correspondence.

subfiles.title: Governor of Hawaii on Hakuyo Maru visit
subfiles.about: Confirms that Hawaii will extend customary courtesies and facilities during the Hakuyo Maru’s proposed visit to Hilo.
subfiles.summary: Governor Poindexter acknowledges notice of the proposed visit to Hilo.

subfiles.title: File note for Yokohama despatch
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Yokohama despatch on the Hakuyo Maru’s gratis Bill of Health.
subfiles.summary: Directs readers to another file for Boyce’s despatch.

subfiles.title: Gratis Bill of Health and crew list visa for Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consulate, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Encloses a memorandum on documents issued to the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Boyce forwards the consular memorandum.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Hakuyo Maru travel documents
subfiles.about: Records Captain Nakakawa’s withdrawal of planned Aleutian port calls to obtain a Bill of Health and crew list visa for Seattle.
subfiles.summary: After being told special permission was needed for closed U.S. ports, Nakakawa dropped those calls. The consul issued documents expressly invalid for closed ports.

subfiles.title: File note for Navy Department letter
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Navy letter about reciprocal vessel visits and suspicions of Pacific fortification.
subfiles.summary: Points to another file for the Navy letter.

subfiles.title: File note for telegram 75
subfiles.about: Cross-references instructions on Japanese and American public-vessel visits to closed harbors.
subfiles.summary: Indexes telegram 75 and its proposed Alden visit.

subfiles.title: Telegram 75 on reciprocal access to closed harbors
subfiles.about: Instructs the ambassador to suggest an invitation for USS Alden to visit ports in Japan’s Mandated Islands.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites U.S. permission for Japanese public vessels to enter closed Alaskan harbors and argues that reciprocal access could ease suspicions about Pacific fortifications. It asks the ambassador to raise the Alden visit informally with Japan’s foreign minister and report by telegraph.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note canceling Hakuho Maru visit
subfiles.about: Reports that engine and hull trouble have forced cancellation of the Hakuho Maru’s proposed Aleutian visit.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador asks that his regrets be conveyed to American authorities.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to Treasury
subfiles.about: Advises Treasury that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Japanese ambassador’s cancellation and regrets.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to War
subfiles.about: Advises War that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Japanese ambassador’s cancellation and regrets.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to Navy
subfiles.about: Advises Navy that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the cancellation and encloses the ambassador’s note.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to Commerce
subfiles.about: Advises Commerce that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Japanese ambassador’s cancellation and regrets.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to Agriculture
subfiles.about: Advises Agriculture that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Japanese ambassador’s cancellation and regrets.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to Interior
subfiles.about: Advises Interior that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Japanese ambassador’s cancellation and regrets.

subfiles.title: Notice of Hakuho Maru cancellation to Labor
subfiles.about: Advises Labor that the Hakuho Maru will not visit Aleutian ports.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Japanese ambassador’s cancellation and regrets.

subfiles.title: Reply to Japanese ambassador on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Acknowledges cancellation of the Hakuho Maru’s Aleutian visit and confirms that the ambassador’s regrets were conveyed.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the ambassador’s note and confirms notification of interested authorities.

subfiles.title: War Department acknowledgment of canceled visit
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Hakuho Maru cancellation and notes that the Ninth Corps Area was informed.
subfiles.summary: War had no jurisdiction over Aleutian ports but forwarded both State letters to its commanding general in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of canceled visit
subfiles.about: Confirms that authorized courtesy privileges for the Hakuho Maru have been discontinued.
subfiles.summary: Treasury is notifying its officers of the cancellation.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Coast Guard reports
subfiles.from: Josephine Roche, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards Coast Guard reports concerning the Hakuyo Maru and other Japanese vessels in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: Lists three enclosed Coast Guard reports.

subfiles.title: Alert report on a Japanese vessel
subfiles.from: Commanding Officer, Coast Guard cutter Alert
subfiles.about: Reports observations of a Japanese vessel in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: The heavily garbled page appears to concern Japanese fishing-vessel activity.

subfiles.title: Bering Sea Patrol official dispatch
subfiles.about: Reports the Hakuyo Maru’s movements and the positions of other Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Garbled dispatch on vessel movements and courtesies extended.

subfiles.title: Cyane report on Hakuyo Maru activities
subfiles.from: J. A. Dirks, Commanding Officer, Cyane
subfiles.about: Describes the Hakuyo Maru’s Kiska Harbor visit, onboard facilities, personnel, and subsequent movements.
subfiles.summary: The Cyane’s boarding officer inspected the training ship, met Captain Nakakawa, and learned about its crew, students, research facilities, and equipment. Students went ashore at Kiska; the Cyane later followed the ship toward Bristol Bay. Endorsements record forwarding the report to Coast Guard and naval authorities.

subfiles.title: Hakuyo Maru cruise schedule
subfiles.about: Sets out the Hakuyo Maru’s planned 1936 cruise, including Japanese, North Pacific, and Alaskan stops.
subfiles.summary: Tabular cruise itinerary, partly illegible in OCR.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Coast Guard reports
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of reports on Japanese vessels in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Treasury for its August 18 transmittal.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing vessels off the Alaskan Coast
subfiles.about: Assesses Japanese research into offshore Bristol Bay salmon fishing and the resulting concern among American packers.
subfiles.summary: The Bureau reviews Japanese crab canneries, fishery research vessels, offshore salmon catches, and Professor Kanda’s suggestion of a joint investigation. It says high-seas salmon fishing is feasible and legally open to Japanese vessels beyond the three-mile limit. It describes industry alarm and attaches a Pacific Fisherman article.

subfiles.title: Protect Our Alaska Salmon from Alien Exploitation
subfiles.about: Argues for diplomatic and industry action to keep foreign vessels from catching Alaska salmon on the high seas.
subfiles.summary: The article warns that Japanese floating canneries and offshore gill nets could intercept Bristol Bay salmon runs, damage American canneries, and undermine conservation. It draws on Japanese experience in Kamchatka, rejects a shared fishery arrangement, and urges the United States to assert exclusive rights to salmon spawned and protected in Alaska.

subfiles.title: Extract from Wrangell warden’s semimonthly report
subfiles.about: Notes a visit by two Japanese company representatives studying Alaska’s salmon industry.
subfiles.summary: Kogi Uchida and Tokuze Suzuki visited the Wrangell office on August 19.

subfiles.title: Name note on Shirotaka Maru
subfiles.about: Suggests that Shirotaka Maru and Hakuho Maru are alternate readings of the same vessel name.
subfiles.summary: Records the proposed name equivalence and says no action is required.
